xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-5170: darwin: skip Linux-only systemctl/journalctl checks (supervisor unit status, OOM canary)

plan.title: darwin: skip Linux-only systemctl/journalctl checks (supervisor unit status, OOM canary)
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: On macOS the restart announcer runs `systemctl --user is-failed overdeck-supervisor.service` on every pass (30 times in the first 30 s, then every 15 s), and the memory-pressure patrol's OOM canary spawns `journalctl -k` once at boot. Neither binary exists on macOS, and each failed spawn there leaves about ten dead node processes (PAN-5168). The canary also writes the full ENOENT error object into the dashboard log.
narratives.Proposal: Add a `process.platform !== 'linux'` early return to `isSupervisorUnitFailed` (src/lib/systemd.ts) and to the OOM canary `readNewKernelJournal` (src/lib/cloister/memory-pressure-patrol.ts), which also now logs one line on a Linux failure. In the restart announcer, Linux keeps the systemd unit-failed path unchanged; every other platform probes the supervisor's `GET /health` instead and emits one error activity row when a supervisor this process has seen answer stays unreachable for 60 s. The rule lives in a pure tracker module (src/dashboard/server/services/supervisor-reachability.ts). Docs D-10 (ANYWHERE-ARCHITECTURE.md), the memory gate (PIPELINE-GATES.md) and changelog.d/pan-5170.md describe the macOS behavior. Full detail in .pan/drafts/PAN-5170.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Guarding `findManagedServerPid` in src/lib/tmux.ts (not a poller; runs only on conversation stop)
- Any host-tool lookup, PATH cache, or ENOENT backoff (PAN-5168 owns it)
- Detecting Linux without systemd or without journalctl ahead of the spawn
- A macOS OOM replacement (kern.memorystatus_vm_pressure_level or JetsamEvent-*.ips)
- A 'supervisor is back' recovery activity row on macOS
- Any launchctl call from the restart announcer
- Writing restart-status.json from the macOS supervisor check
- Changing Linux behavior of the unit-failed check, the restart-status write, or the GAVE UP row
- Changing isSupervisorUnitActive, systemdUserAvailable, or any other systemd.ts function

autoDecisions.summary: Guard by `process.platform !== 'linux'` only; no 'systemd is present' probe on Linux.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue lists the systemd-presence check as optional; on Linux a failed spawn costs one process, and the issue comment forbids a second tool cache because PAN-5168 owns host-tool lookup.

autoDecisions.summary: On macOS, report supervisor liveness via HTTP GET /health on the supervisor port, not the pidfile.
autoDecisions.rationale: Only startSupervisorProcess writes supervisor.pid; a launchd-run supervisor (pan connect) has none, so a pidfile check would report a healthy supervisor dead. The HTTP probe covers both launch modes and starts no child process. The issue comment allows 'pidfile or liveness'.

autoDecisions.summary: Report the macOS supervisor down only after this process has seen it answer once and it then stays unreachable for 60 s; once per episode.
autoDecisions.rationale: Plain `node dist/dashboard/server.js` runs have no supervisor, pan reload/restart cycle it, and launchd restarts after a 5 s throttle; none of these should raise an error row.

autoDecisions.summary: The macOS path emits an activity row directly and writes no restart-status.json.
autoDecisions.rationale: The systemd status text (attempts: 3, restart limit, GAVE UP) is wrong for macOS; a direct emit keeps the Linux restart-status semantics untouched.
The issue comment limits the change to the two named checks; it is not a poller, and the parallel tmux work may touch that file.

Add the pure supervisor reachability tracker with its 60 s down window

narrative.Action: PRD WI-2. Create src/dashboard/server/services/supervisor-reachability.ts exactly as the PRD snippet: export `SUPERVISOR_DOWN_WINDOW_MS = 60_000`, `interface SupervisorDownReport { unreachableForMs: number }`, `interface SupervisorReachabilityTracker { observe(answered: boolean, nowMs: number): SupervisorDownReport | null }`, and `createSupervisorReachabilityTracker(windowMs = SUPERVISOR_DOWN_WINDOW_MS)`. Rule: a success sets seenAlive, clears the unreachable timer and the reported latch, returns null; a failure before any success returns null; the first failure after a success starts the timer at nowMs; return a report once when nowMs - start >= windowMs, then null until a success resets. Pure: no timers, no I/O, no imports beyond types. Write the four test cases listed in PRD WI-2 in src/dashboard/server/services/__tests__/supervisor-reachability.test.ts using explicit nowMs values.

items.title: Given the tracker has never seen a success, when observe(false, t) is called for t from 0 to 600000, then every call returns null

Given a reported episode, when observe(true, t) is followed by 61 s of failures, then the tracker returns a second report
Given success at 0, failure at 1000, success at 30000, when failures occur at 40000 and 90000, then both return null because the timer restarted at 40000

In src/dashboard/server/services/restart-announcer.ts: import createSupervisorReachabilityTracker and the tracker type from './supervisor-reachability.js' and getSupervisorUrl from '../../../lib/supervisor.js'. Add optional deps `platform?: NodeJS.Platform`, `probeSupervisor?: () => Promise<boolean>`, `supervisorUrl?: () => string` to RestartAnnouncerDeps. Add a module-level tracker that stopRestartAnnouncer() replaces with a fresh one, a module-level memoized default URL (`cachedSupervisorUrl ??= getSupervisorUrl()`), and `probeSupervisorHealth(url)` that fetches `${url}/health` with an AbortController + setTimeout(2000, unref'd, cleared in finally) and returns res.ok, false on any error. In announceNewRestart, replace the `await syncSupervisorUnitFailureStatus(...)` line with a branch: platform === 'linux' runs it unchanged; any other platform runs checkSupervisorReachable, which calls the probe (rejection = false), feeds tracker.observe(answered, now()), and on a report emits { source: 'supervisor', level: 'error', desktop: false, message: `The supervisor at ${url} has not answered for ${Math.floor(ms/1000)} s. Force Restart and the dashboard watchdog do not work until it runs again. Run \`pan up\` to start it.` }. The non-Linux branch never calls readSupervisorUnitFailed or writeStatus. Add one sentence about the macOS branch to the module header. Do not use AbortSignal.timeout, skipIf, or source-reading tests.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-4. In src/lib/cloister/memory-pressure-patrol.ts, export `interface KernelJournalDeps { platform: NodeJS.Platform; runJournalctl: (args: string[]) => Promise<string>; warn: (line: string) => void }` and make `readNewKernelJournal(deps: Partial<KernelJournalDeps> = {})` exported. First statement: `if ((deps.platform ?? process.platform) !== 'linux') return '';` (before the disabled check, the cursor stat, the spawn, or any log). The default runJournalctl wraps the existing `promisify(execFile)('journalctl', args, { timeout: 10000 })` and returns stdout; keep the cursor-file and `-n 0` logic unchanged. Replace the catch's console.warn(error object) with one string: `[memory-pressure-patrol] OOM canary disabled: journalctl failed (${String(code ?? message ?? err)})` passed to deps.warn (default `console.warn(line)`), then disable the canary. In patrolMemoryPressure change the default to `deps.readNewKernelJournal || (() => readNewKernelJournal())`. Update the function's doc comment to say Linux only (PAN-5170). Add describe('readNewKernelJournal (PAN-5170)') in tests/unit/lib/cloister/memory-pressure-patrol.test.ts with the four cases in PRD WI-4, calling __resetMemoryPressurePatrolState() in beforeEach.
